newsitem.title: GERMANY: SIEMENS SAYS "NO NEGOTIATIONS WITH GEC" ON GPT. [CORRECTED 18:00 GMT]
newsitem.headline: SIEMENS SAYS "NO NEGOTIATIONS WITH GEC" ON GPT. [CORRECTED 18:00 GMT]

text.p: Siemens AG said on Wednesday that one of its senior executives had mistakenly told reporters the company was negotiating with Britain's GEC about buying GEC's stake in their GPT telecommunications venture.
"There are currently no negotiations with GEC."
(Company corrects statement by one of its executives to show that there are currently no talks with GEC on its GPT stake).
When asked whether the executive had been misunderstood by reporters the spokesman said, "No, the mistake was ours."

During a news conference in Munich, Siemens director of the private networks division, Dietrich Botsch, told reporters the company was negotiating with General Electric Co Plc about buying GEC's 60 percent stake in their telecommunications joint venture GPT.
Botsch said Siemens already had an option to buy the shares after the year 2000.
"GEC is interested in doing that sooner," he said.
Asked whether Siemens was interested in the GEC stake in GPT, he said: "Yes, that is currently being negotiated."

Botsch added that it was conceivable that the deal could include a swap of Siemens' security technology business for the GPT shares, but whether the deal was concluded in the end would be a "question of price".
Siemens said on Tuesday that there would be no changes to the shareholdings in the GPT venture following a reorganisation at GEC.
GEC had unveiled its long awaited strategic blueprint to take it into the next century, putting defence at the heart of the group and signalling a possible float of its rail/power joint venture.
Managing director George Simpson said GEC was also considering "repositioning" its telecoms joint venture GPT.
Simpson said he had thought about selling the telecoms stake, but rejected it.

"Clearly one option was to sell our stake to Siemens. But I am driven by shareholder value. We will monitor the business and rewrite the charter for that business, as telecoms is a high growth area which GEC should remain in," he said.
